summary: Calculates inverse-kinematics solutions for Bone objects and outputs rotations that can be exported back to a bone chain.
key_concepts: Calculates inverse kinematics simulations for Bone objects and legacy object-level bone chains.
Solver Type switches between no solve, rest display, capture display, inverse kinematics, constraints, and curve-following modes.
Inverse Kinematics mode positions the end of the chain at the origin of the End Affector object.
Rest angles shape the IK solution, and continuity is only guaranteed for a fixed set of rest angles.
Twist Affector and IK Twist control chain twist around the root-to-end-affector axis.
Solved rotation channels are intended to be exported back to the bone chain rather than mixed with manual bone rotations.

key_params.name: solvertype
key_params.note: None, rest position, capture position, inverse kinematics, constraint, or curve mode

key_params.name: endaffector
key_params.note: Target object for the end of the chain

key_params.name: curve
key_params.note: Use curve solver or curve object control

common_gotchas: Inverse Kin CHOP works with Bone objects and legacy object-level rigging.
Do not animate rest angles casually because IK continuity is only guaranteed for a fixed rest-angle set.
Enable the export flag to drive the bones with the solved rotation channels.
Inverse Kinematics mode requires an End Affector object.
Follow Curve mode requires a curve object and should not be planned like end-affector IK.
